glossary_explaination: Applies a set of chosen settings to the calculation and evaluation system.
Ability that changes the specs of the character’s attack.
Role given to units that Restores the base's HP, crucial for surviving long waves.
Ability that prevents mobs from crossing the base for a certain period of time.
Ability that boost one or more statistics of characters placed around this character.
% bonus applied by the main buff (Erwin, Brook, Idol, etc.). It is applied to both dot and pure hit damages.
Role given to units that increases the stats or abilities of nearby units.
Role given to units that excels at holding specific positions, providing area control.
The star diagram is composed of two values: the ranking in the list of characters, and the pure value of the statistic. This parameter indicates the share (in %) assigned to the ranking.
Changes from a linear scale (1, 2, 3, 4) to a logarithmic scale (1, 10, 100, 1000) for the diagram calculation ratios.
Role given to units that can resets or reduces cooldowns, allowing for more frequent ability use.
Passive ability that after a number of attacks : performs a more powerful attack.
Role given to units that specializes in controlling large groups of enemies.
Ability that inflicts damage based on mob lives/ Reduces mobs lives to a certain percentage.
Ability that inflicts damage over time (passive or active), like bleeding, burn, poison.
Considers how the unit’s enchantment type (e.g. Fire, Water, etc.) interacts with enemy weaknesses or resistances.
Passive ability that allows the unit to replace enemies enchants by the weak enchant for the unit (ONLY if it already has a enchant).
Role given to units that deals high damage to finish off weakened enemies efficiently. It's also the default role.

glossary_name: Also known as FD. Evaluates how hard it is to obtain or evolve a unit, including materials, time, and event availability.
glossary_explaination: Evaluates how hard it is to obtain or evolve a unit, including materials, time, and event availability.
Filters or adjusts stats based on the game mode (e.g., Raid, Infinite, Placement only, etc.), as some units perform better in certain modes.
Ability that blocks the advance of mobs for a long period of time. Cannot be spammed.
Ability that restores life to the base/ Increases the life capacity of the base.
Loads a previously saved preset (by its given ID or name) to restore your custom settings.
Controls how much the Area of Effect type (Circle, Cone, Line, etc.) impacts the unit’s range ranking.
Ability that makes money.
Ability that does instant damage to mobs.
Role give to units that are really expensive to place but rewarding in high start dps output.
Indicates the percentage of damage attributed to all characters in a single category (from the first unit of the team).
Indicates the cost reduction of characters in a single category (from the first unit of the team).
Indicates how much Damage-over-Time (burn, bleed, etc.) boost is granted by unit in the leader slot.
Refers to the number of times a unit can be placed on the map at once.
Role given to units that divides by a certain % the health of mobs, making them easier to defeat.
Role given to units that manipulates enemy movement or stunning, controlling the battlefield. It's also the name given to abilities that can manipulates enemy movement or placement.
Role given to units that generates additional cash each wave to support expensive strategies.
Ability that does one-time instant damage to mobs.
Ability that  does one-time damage based on mobs lives or that reduces mobs health to a certain percentage.
Role give to units that delivers massive burst damage, often with infinite cooldowns.
Passive ability that increases the damage of the character each wave.
Ability that removes some attributes from mobs.
Role given to units that removes title to enemies, allowing units to target them, and remove their abilities.
Ability that drives back the mobs.
Describes the unit’s primary function — such as DPS, support, debuffer, farm, etc.
Saves your current settings/filters to be reused later. Helpful for switching between playstyles or gamemodes. You must remember the ID that will be given to you
Ability that allows an unit to boost itself.
Refers to all the customizable options in the ASTD ranking/chart system. Allows you to define what matters most to you.
Role given to units that reduces the speed of enemies, giving more time to attack. Also, ability that slows the enemies movement.
Role given to units that can barely solo certain gamemodes.
Special ability that cannot be classified.
Role given to units that provides unique or niche buffs that can significantly impact certain strategies (maybe).
Includes unique effects like bleed, burn, poison, freeze, etc., and how much bonus damage they contribute overall.
Ability that pauses the character.
Role given to units that strong early game units with low cost, perfect for initial waves.
Ability that blocks the mobs advance for a long period of time. Can be spammed.
Ability that spawns mobs on your side of the path. Inflict damage on mobs.
Role given to units that spawns mobs on the track to assist in combat.
Indicates the targeting options a unit has — e.g. Air, Ground, Both, Air-only, etc.
Ability that teleports the mobs back.
Ability that spawns laying traps that deals damage.
Defines the current level of the unit, which affects its base stats. Usually assumed to be max level for calculations.
Role given to units that spawns additional units to assist in combat.
Describes how quickly and efficiently a unit gains power as you upgrade it. Units with strong early upgrades are often favored.
Define how much dps the unit deals per $ of investment.
Relevance of the cost/dps increase of the different levels of upgrades.
